sections.title: Ancient Wars, Modern Tools: The Evolution of Antiviral Immunity and its Applications
sections.description: Fundamental insights into antiviral defense systems and mechanisms, like CRISPR-Cas and RNA silencing, have been repurposed for genetic engineering, diagnostics, and research tools that transformed science and medicine. We will critically analyze classic and recent papers on the discovery and application of antiviral defense systems in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. We will focus on the biochemical, structural and molecular biology techniques used to uncover how these systems work. In a journal club format, students will present primary research articles and lead vigorous discussions. Our goal is to learn how protein- and nucleic acid-based molecular machines distinguish “self” from “non-self” and mount response, and how these naturally evolved mechanisms can be repurposed for biomedicine.
